To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a supramolecular metal complex with an extended pi-electron system, Ru-V(2)(6), was synthesized; (b) the complex exhibits long-lived charge separation upon photoexcitation of the Ru moiety; (c) the complex is capable of photocleaving plasmid DNA in both air and under N2 atmosphere, and that the mechanism of photocleavage involves a radical mechanism.

a novel Ru(II)-linked viologen complex was synthesized, and the complex was shown to photocleave plasmid DNA through the generation of a long-lived charge-separation state, which is independent of the presence of oxygen.
the photocleavage reaction of a plasmid DNA is observed upon irradiation of the Ru-V(1)-(2+), which is a novel Ru(II)-linked viologen complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of supramolecular Ru(bpy)(2)(2+) photosensitizers with a view to the design of efficient photocleaving agents for DNA.
the development of novel supramolecular Ru-photosensitizer complexes that are capable of generating reactive oxygen species upon irradiation, as well as those that do not.

the development of supramolecular Ru complexes that are designed to undergo photoinduced electron transfer (PET) and/or energy transfer (ET) reactions and to use these reactions for the development of novel photofunctional systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ru(II)-Vi complex, Ru-V(2)-V(1)(2+), is a novel and efficient DNA photocleaving agent that operates through the photoinduced electron transfer (PET) mechanism.

the photocleavage is due to the formation of the long-lived charge-separated state, which is formed upon excitation of the metal complex and is responsible for the DNA photocleavage, rather than the formation of reactive species, such as O(2)(-) and (1)O2, that are formed in the presence of O(2).
the photocleavage by Ru-V(2) is not mediated by (1)O2, and the mechanism of the DNA photocleavage by the Ru-V(2)(6+)/V(2)(.)+ system is not fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ru-V(1) -V(2)(2+) is a supramolecular complex that is able to generate a long-lived charge separated state, Ru(II)-V(2.+/1+), which in turn is able to cleave DNA.
the photocleavage is not caused by reactive oxygen species but is due to the long-lived charge-separated state of the complex.
the photocleavage by Ru(II)-V(1)-V2(6+) is not mediated by the reactive oxygen species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ru-V(1)-(V(2))(6+) complex can be used for the photocleavage DNA in the absence of oxygen.
a supramolecular complex of Ru(II)-linked viologens is capable of DNA photocleavage.
Ru-V(1) -V(2)(+) is a new photocleaving agent that is active both in air and in the absence of O(2).
